title: FAMILY | 5.24.26 The Life and Legacy of Eddie Rickenbacker
author: The Ways of a Gentleman
summary: Eddie Rickenbacker (1890-1973) embodied a version of American character forged entirely through self-directed effort. Born the third of eight children in a working-class Columbus, Ohio family, he left school after his father's death but educated himself through correspondence courses while working, rising to department head by 16 and managing automobile sales across four states by 19. On the racing circuit he was known as 'Fast Eddie,' competing in the Indianapolis 500 four times. In World War I he retrained as a pilot and became America's Ace of Aces: 26 enemy aircraft downed, over 300 combat hours flown, the Distinguished Service Cross eight times (one upgraded to the Medal of Honor). Post-war he authored a bestselling memoir, founded Florida Airways, purchased the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, and transformed Eastern Air Lines into the most profitable U.S. airline. In World War II his B-17 crash-landed in the Pacific; he and his crew survived 24 days adrift on rafts. He passed away in Switzerland in 1973 at 82, memorialized in Rickenbacker International Airport in Columbus. The article draws lessons for the 'modern gentleman': that character, grit, and discipline built through adversity endure where surface presentations fade.
points: * Rickenbacker left school after his father's death but educated himself through correspondence engineering courses while working, becoming a department head at 16 and managing automobile sales across four states by 19 -- self-directed learning as survival strategy. * As America's Ace of Aces in WWI he downed 26 enemy aircraft, flew over 300 combat hours (more than any other U.S. pilot), received the Distinguished Service Cross eight times, and had one award upgraded to the Medal of Honor. * Post-war entrepreneurship spanned multiple domains: bestselling war memoir, Rickenbacker Motor Company, purchase of the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, founding of Florida Airways, and the presidency of Eastern Air Lines -- one of the most successful airlines in the country under his leadership. * In 1942, his B-17 crash-landed in the Pacific on a WWII mission to deliver a secret message to General MacArthur; Rickenbacker and his crew survived 24 days adrift on life rafts, living on rainwater and raw fish, before completing the mission upon rescue. * Rickenbacker died in 1973 at 82, leaving behind Rickenbacker International Airport in Columbus, a formula for success ('Think things through, then follow through'), and a career arc from fatherless boy to Medal of Honor recipient to airline CEO.
quotes: I can give you a six-word formula for success: Think things through, then follow through. -- Eddie Rickenbacker
Even without formal schooling, Eddie's thirst for knowledge didn't falter. While working at a car company, he took correspondence courses in engineering and quickly rose through the ranks.
